name: Fudgy Protein Brownies
description: The fudge-maximized protein brownie — the original of a three-texture set, finished smooth (uniformly fudgy) or chunky (sweetened dark-chocolate pockets). Fudge comes from butter + a little unsweetened baking chocolate, with the egg barely beaten and stirred in last to keep air out (air bakes cakey). Cocoa + espresso are bloomed in the warm fat; sweetener is 1/4 cup granulated Splenda (never monk fruit). Bakes at 325F for ~18 min, pulled at a slight center jiggle, then cooled fully and chilled — better the next day. Computed ~630 cal / 38 g protein per batch of 9; ~70 cal, 4.2P, 7.2C, 3.4F per square; 16.5 cal per g protein. Large egg (50 g). Source: user.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 325°F (165°C) and line or grease a small ~6-inch square pan.
Melt the butter + baking chocolate over low heat or in short microwave bursts. Stir in the cocoa + espresso powder to bloom them in the warm fat — it becomes a thick paste.

Stir in the skim milk to loosen and finish blooming; warm gently to combine. For chunky brownies, reserve 1–2 tsp of the thick paste, stir a pinch of Splenda into it, and set aside. Off the heat, cool to just warm.
Stir in the Splenda, then the Greek yogurt and vanilla.

Lightly beat the egg and egg white together (no whipping — keep air out so it bakes fudgy, not cakey) and stir in last. If the base is still warm, temper first: stir a spoonful of base into the egg, then add it back.

Whisk the flour + cornstarch + protein powder + salt, then fold into the batter by hand just until no dry streaks remain — then stop. A few small lumps are fine; mixing past this develops gluten and bakes up cakey. Smooth finish: fold uniform. Chunky finish: fold in the reserved sweetened paste at the very end so it stays in pockets. Spread in the pan.
Bake at 325°F for ~18 minutes, checking from ~14. Pull at a slight center jiggle (not a liquid slosh) — it should look a touch underdone; carryover heat and cooling finish the set.

Doneness: edges set and just pulling from the sides with a slight wobble in the center (not a liquid slosh). A toothpick should read moist crumbs clinging — a clean toothpick means overbaked. On these small protein batters, trust the jiggle over the toothpick.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, undisturbed — never cut warm. The crumb sets and the protein firms as it cools; a warm one seems gummy and then comes good.

Chill a few hours or overnight — they're better the next day. Cut cold with a clean knife (for the fudgy ones, run it under hot water and wipe between cuts). Store airtight; freeze portions for longer keeping. Optional: microwave a piece 8–10 sec to soften the fat — no longer, or the protein turns rubbery.

notes.text: Don't whip the egg — just break the yolk and stir it in gently. Beating in air makes the batter puff in the oven and bake cakey; keeping it still keeps it dense and fudgy.
The cocoa blooms in warm butter + baking chocolate — let the fat cool to just warm (not hot) before adding the egg in step b5, or the egg scrambles. It should feel comfortable to touch.
18 min at 325°F is the max; start checking at 14 min. Pull at a slight center jiggle — not liquid, but not fully set. The protein continues cooking off-heat and the fudgy window closes fast.
If reheating a square, microwave 8–10 sec only — any longer and the protein in the Greek yogurt turns grainy and rubbery. Pull while it still feels just warm.
Stop folding the moment no dry streaks remain; the batter is small and 15 g of protein powder makes it easy to over-develop gluten. Extra strokes bake out the fudge into a tight, cakey crumb.

Sweetness pass: this base carries THREE bitter sources (cocoa + unsweetened baking chocolate + chocolate protein powder), which mask sweetness - chocolate bakes need ~20-30% more sweetener than vanilla ones to read equally sweet. Cocoa cut 33->20g, Splenda up to 6 tbsp, vanilla up to 1 tsp. The bloom paste in b2/b3 will be a little looser with less cocoa - fine. If STILL bitter, swap the baking chocolate for semi-sweet chips before adding more Splenda.

Fat cut (untested vs the excellent-rated bake): butter halved 20->10g with +20g Greek yogurt backfill; whole egg kept on purpose (yolk = emulsion + the remaining fudge fat). Bloom paste in b2 will be tighter with half the butter - loosen with the milk in b3 as needed. If this bake loses the fudge, restore butter to 20g before touching anything else; do NOT push the fat cut down to the chewy variants until this is tasted.

Protein raised to a full 35g chocolate-powder serving + 33g egg white (~56g protein/batch). That's past the variants' proven 30g - highest whey load yet in this family, so rubber watch is ON: bake gentle (325F, pull at slight jiggle from 14 min) and never overbake. Milk trimmed 40->25ml since the white adds liquid; add a splash back if the batter is stiff. If this bake turns bouncy, drop powder back toward 25-27g FIRST - protein powder, not the egg white, is the rubber source.
